subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Which of the following options is the most appropriate?

options.text: There is no registration requirement for copyright
Trade Marks may or may not be registered
The Register of Trade Marks keeps a record of all copyright
Copyright is registered according to its category

explanation: In Nigeria copyright protection arises automatically upon creation; no formal registration is required.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: All these are primary sources of Business Law in Nigeria, except............
explanation: Delegated or subsidiary legislation is considered secondary; primary sources are the Constitution, statutes and judicial precedents.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Which of these is a feature of hire-purchase transaction?

options.text: Always treated as employees of the owner
Agent of the owner is the Hirer’s agent
Forcibly taking possession of the Hired goods

explanation: A hallmark of hire‑purchase is that the hirer has an option to purchase the goods at the end of the payment period.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: An offer can be made expressly or by….........
explanation: An offer may be implied by the conduct of a party, not just by explicit words.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Corporate Social Responsibility benefits the company/business in which of the following ways?
explanation: CSR can improve financial performance, strengthen brand reputation and facilitate access to capital, so all listed benefits are correct.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: The doctrine of ‘privity’ of contract posits that ……

options.text: Only two people can benefit from a contract.
Contracts can be enforced only when it is between two people.
Only parties to a contract can enforce it or have it enforced against them
Only the offeror can enforce or rescind the contract.

explanation: Privity of contract means that only the parties who have entered into the contract have rights and obligations under it.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Identify the type of remedy in which specific performance is central to.
explanation: Specific performance is an equitable remedy, compelling a party to perform its contractual obligations.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Which of the following options exemplifies the meaning of the Latin maxim caveat emptor ?
explanation: "Caveat emptor" translates to "let the buyer beware".

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Unqualified expression of assent to the exact terms of an offer is regarded as ….
explanation: An unqualified acceptance of all the terms of an offer creates a binding contract.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Which Court has Jurisdiction to hear matters on infringement of copy right?
explanation: In Nigeria, the Federal High Court has jurisdiction over copyright infringement matters.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: The Court that has Jurisdiction on taxation and Customs and Excise is the …………

options.text: High Court of the Federal Capital Territory

explanation: Taxation, customs and excise matters are within the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court in Nigeria.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Which is the odd one among these the following?
explanation: Denotative Rule is not a recognized rule of statutory interpretation, unlike the other three.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Offer is central to contract because the ……………….. define(s) the obligations of parties to it.
explanation: The terms of the offer set out the rights and duties of the contracting parties.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: All these are primary sources of business law, except the combination of ……………

options.text: Employees’ Hand Book and Judicial Precedents

explanation: An Employees’ Hand Book is a secondary source; primary sources include legislation, judicial precedent, customary and common law.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Which of these is a feature of hire‑purchase transaction?

options.text: Always treated as employees of the owner
Agent of the owner is the Hire’s agent
Forcibly taking possession of the hired goods

explanation: A hire‑purchase agreement typically includes an option for the hirer to purchase the goods at the end of the payment period.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Consideration must therefore flow from the ………….
explanation: In contract law, consideration must be provided by the promisee (the party who receives the promise) to the promisor.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: The law which defines a bank as a person who carries out banking business is ……..
explanation: The Banking Act of 1969 is the principal legislation that defines a bank as a person carrying on banking business in Nigeria.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: The Nigerian Industrial Development Bank was established in …….
explanation: The Nigerian Industrial Development Bank (NIDB) was founded in 1964 as a development finance institution.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: A joint contribution of funds by two or more merchant banks to assist a corporate organisation seeking financial assistance is called …………. loan.
explanation: When several banks pool resources to lend to a single borrower, the arrangement is known as a syndicated loan.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Section 13 of the Sale of Goods Act deals with…………..
explanation: Section 13 of the Sale of Goods Act imposes an implied condition that goods must correspond with the description under which they are sold.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: Assuming A wants to sue B, he will be doing that to recover...............?
explanation: When a party breaches a contract, the injured party typically sues for damages to compensate for the loss suffered, which is the appropriate remedy here.

subject: Elements of Nigeria's Business Law and Legal System
stem: The money paid by C is known in law as...............
explanation: In contract law, the payment made by one party in exchange for the other party's performance constitutes consideration, the essential element of a binding agreement.
